questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

We should always remember not to ________ any problems and issues that may affect our career in any organisation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**create**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The meaning of the given words**__:

 
 
• **affect**: to have an effect on
 
• **undertake**: to engage in
 
• **inflict**: to force someone to experience something unpleasant
 
• **create**: to give rise to something
 
 
 
• Both the words, i.e. '**affect**' and '**undertake**' are inappropriate for the given sentence.
 
• Hence, **options 1)** and **2)** should be eliminated.
 
• The meaning of the word '**inflict**' shows that we cannot choose it for this sentence.
 
• One may give rise to a problem. Therefore, '**create**' is the only word which fits here well.
 
• Hence, **option 4) **is the answer.

options.text: After you will be returning from

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**After you return from**'.

__
 
• The given is a **conditional sentence** as the **principal clause**(*I will come and meet you*.) is written in **simple future tense**.
 
• Therefore, **simple present tense** should be used in the **subordinate clause**(*After you will return from Bangalore*,).
 
• Hence, '**will**' should be removed from the **subordinate clause**.
 
• So, 'After you return from' can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

**Correct sentence**__: *After you return from Bangalore, I will come and meet yo*u.

The sentence which __expresses a condition is called a conditional sentence__.

__
 
• **Example:**__ She will not go to meet you if you don't invite her.

questions.question:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**from this financial year**'.

__
 
• The segment '**from this financial year**' is grammatically incorrect.
 
• 'Budgets' are planned '**for**' a certain period.
 
• Hence, the preposition '**from**' is incorrect and it should be replaced with the preposition '**for**'.

**Correct sentence**__: *The government’s interim budget for this financial year contained several measures which have the forthcoming elections in mind.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 A **preposition** shows the relationship of a __noun or a pronoun to another word__.

__
 
• **Example**__: *He is sitting on the chair.

 I was standing before the judge*.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Is it true that the students from the Space Research Centre _________ this evening?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e. 'are arriving'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The blank in the given sentence is to be filled with the present continuous tense as it describes an action that is planned for the near future.
 
• The subject in the sentence "students" is plural, which means the verb should also be in a plural form. 
 
• Therefore, the correct form of the verb here is "are arriving".
 
 
• **Example:** The guests are arriving at the party in the evening.
 
 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *Is it true that the students from the Space Research Centre **are arriving** this evening?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Is arriving** : The incorrect form as "students" is a plural subject.

 
 
• **Example: **The train is arriving at the station in a few minutes.
 
 
 
• **Has arriving**: Incorrect as "has" does not properly combine with "arriving".
 
 
• **Example: **He has arrived at the airport. (Correct usage would be "has arrived")
 
 
 
• **Have arriving**: Incorrect combination of auxiliary 'have' with 'arriving'.
 
 
• **Example: **The guests have arrived. (Correct usage would be "have arrived")
